html:
Vasco Núñez de Balboa was a Spanish conquistador who, on 25 September 1513, became the first European to see the Pacific Ocean from the Americas, after crossing the isthmus of Panama.

He had escaped his debts in Hispaniola by hiding in a ship's barrel, and rose to lead the settlement of Santa María la Antigua del Darién, the first lasting Spanish town on the mainland. Hearing from Indigenous people of a great sea to the south, he crossed the jungles of Darién with Spanish soldiers and local guides, and claimed the South Sea for Spain.

A rival governor, Pedrarias Dávila, had him beheaded on a false charge of treason in 1519. His discovery opened the way to Pizarro's conquest of Peru, launched from Panama. Panama's currency, the balboa, bears his name.
